help_source.Implanner/Help/1-basics/01-what-implanne: Automation can be switched off entirely, and every step it takes shows up in the same bills and operation lists you already use.

- Build a **plan**: the set of implants a colonist should end up with.
- **Enlist** colonists into plans on the Overview tab.
- **Automation** crafts missing implants, reserves the items, and queues the operations when everything is ready.
Implanner plans colonist implants and automates the work needed to install them.
help_source.Implanner/Help/1-basics/02-overview-tabl: Click a colonist's name to open their details on the right.
The Overview tab lists every colonist who could receive implants.

The S and M columns show Shooting and Melee skill; the small icons show the equipped weapon and belt item. The skill values and belt are informational. In ASAP mode, colonist priority comes first. Among colonists at equal priority who need the same implant, legs go to the slowest; arms prefer an equipped melee weapon, then the highest sum of Crafting and Intellectual skill levels.
![Overview rows with plan, progress, priority and state columns](overview-rows.png)

- **Plan** assigns a colonist to a plan. Click for the menu, or click and drag down the column to paint the same plan onto several colonists.
- **Priority** decides who automation serves first, from First to Last. It can also be painted down the column.
- **Progress** counts installed implants against the plan.
- **State** condenses the colonist's plan status into one word.
help_source.Implanner/Help/1-basics/03-colonist-deta: ![The details panel listing each implant with its status](colonist-details.png)
Select a colonist in the table and the details panel shows every implant in their plan with its current status:

- **Missing**: still needed, nothing reserved yet.
- **Reserved**: an item in storage is claimed for this colonist. Surgery starts once everything the colonist needs next is reserved and on site (see [how automation works](topic:how-automation-works)).
- **Ready**: the reserved item has arrived at the colonist's colony.
- **Surgery scheduled**: the operation is on the colonist's bill list.
- **Recovering**: surgery waits while the colonist is bleeding, has untreated wounds, or is down. Anesthetic sleep does not count.
- **Blocked by doctor floor**: no doctor at the colony meets the required Medicine skill (see [surgery options](topic:surgery-options)).
- **Complete**: installed.
A plan describes an end state: implants the colonist already has count as complete.
help_source.Implanner/Help/1-basics/04-progress-and-:
- **Waiting**: implants are missing, but no item is reserved for this colonist yet.
- **Preparing**: items are reserved and being collected for the colonist's next surgery.
- **Operating**: surgery is scheduled on the colonist's bill list.
- **Done**: every planned implant is installed.
- **Away**: the colonist is off traveling; automation waits.

Progress always reflects what is installed right now. A planned implant the colonist's body cannot take at all (the required part does not exist on it) is left out of their target and counts neither as installed nor as missing. A harvested or destroyed implant counts as missing again, and automation pursues a replacement. If you want to harvest an implant to sell or pass along, switch **Enable automation** off first, or the part will be reserved and scheduled straight back in.
The State column condenses each colonist into one word:

Manually installed implants count too. A superior part installed where the plan wanted a lesser one satisfies that slot: an archotech leg covers a bionic-leg goal, and Implanner never schedules a downgrade. Implants that can share a part, like brain implants, stay separate goals.
help_source.Implanner/Help/2-plans/01-creating-plans: Each card in the plan list shows the plan's implant count, how many colonists are enlisted, and their combined progress.
![The new plan prompt with the Extends selector](newplan-dialog.png)
![Two plan cards with counts and progress bars](plan-cards.png)
On the Plans tab, **New plan** asks for a name and, optionally, a plan to extend.

A plan that **extends** another inherits all of its selections. Build an "Essentials" plan with the implants everyone should have, then extend it into "Miner" or "Farmer" plans that add their own picks or override inherited ones. Edit the base plan and every extending plan follows.
help_source.Implanner/Help/2-plans/02-picking-implan: Some mods upgrade an installed bionic in place, like the modular bionics from Integrated Implants. The upgraded version is listed as its own implant. Picking it overrides the plain version in the plan. A colonist without the plain version receives it first, then the upgrade surgery. A colonist who already has the plain version only needs the upgrade.
![The implant picker with region filter and slot checkboxes](picker-tree.png)
![The requirement prompt for a leg module](requirement-prompt.png)
The middle column lists implants discovered from vanilla, the expansions and every mod, grouped by the body part they target.

Downgrades such as peg legs cannot be planned. Implants with a drawback or a narrow use are also left out: joywire, painstopper, power claw and pilot assistant. Implants only ghouls can take are never listed. Purchase-only parts such as archotech implants, whose item no workbench can craft, are hidden until **Show purchase-only implants** on the Options tab is switched on. An archotech part the player installs manually still counts for the slot it occupies, whether the option is on or off. A planned purchase-only implant never holds up the other implants in a batch, and it is installed with the next batch once the item is in stock. A mod that adds a crafting recipe makes the implant an ordinary one.
![The picker search showing every leg implant in one flat list](picker-search.png)

- The **Limbs / Torso / Head** row filters the list to one body region.
- The search field beside it looks across every region. Typing shows one flat list of the implants and body parts that match. Clear the field or click a region to return to the grouped view.
- Paired parts get one entry per side: a bionic leg (left) and a bionic leg (right) are separate picks.
- Tick a checkbox to add the slot to the plan. Click and drag across checkboxes to select a whole run of slots.
- Hover any entry for its stats and market value.

Some modded implants, like the limb modules from Bionic modularity, can only be installed on an artificial part. Ticking one of these while the plan has no matching replacement opens a prompt listing the replacements that could host it. **Add to plan** adds your choice and the implant together. **Cancel** adds nothing.
help_source.Implanner/Help/2-plans/03-conflicts-and-: ![Rows warning that selecting them overrides the planned bionic arm](picker-overrides.png)
Slots covered by a base plan show an "inherited" caption. Ticking an inherited slot adds it again as this plan's own pick.

Two implants cannot always share a body. One part holds one replacement, some implants exclude each other outright, and some remove a rival wherever it sits, like the mechanite strains from [FSF] Advanced Bionics Expansion. Modules that mount on a bionic limb, like those from Bionic modularity, share the part with the bionic instead of replacing it. Implanner applies the same rules as the game and resolves conflicts when you click.

- Selecting a slot that conflicts with one of the plan's own picks deselects the existing pick. The row warns with an "overrides" caption before you click. A caption too long for the row keeps its end, and hovering it shows the full text.
- In an extending plan, a conflicting inherited slot is suppressed instead: the base plan keeps its choice, your plan overrides it.
The **Mod compatibility** options on the Options tab add two rules the game's data cannot express; see [mod options](topic:mod-options).
![Star tiers with implants ranked from highest to normal priority](tier-panel.png)
Rankings are never changed automatically. Every implant starts at three stars and stays there until you move it.
The right column ranks the plan's own picks into five star tiers; an inherited implant is ranked on its base plan. Drag a row onto another tier to move it.

- Implants in better tiers are reserved and delivered first under the default iteration strategy (see [surgery options](topic:surgery-options)).
- Production queues crafting for better tiers first.
help_source.Implanner/Help/2-plans/05-minimum-qualit:
- New surgeries use the lowest quality the plan accepts, so the better items stay free.
- A better item goes to the highest-priority colonist whose implant of the same kind is worse. Their old implant is removed first, then the better one is installed, and the removed implant goes to the next colonist in line.
- An item already reserved for a lower-priority colonist is handed over too, as long as their surgery is not scheduled yet.
A colonist who already has the planned implant keeps it, even below the minimum, unless the option below is switched on.
![The plan header with the Minimum quality button](plan-min-quality.png)
When Implanner crafts an implant for the plan:

- With Quality Jobs loaded, the crafting bill targets the minimum, so the finishing step goes to a crafter who can reach it.
- A hybrid implant from Vanilla Genetics Expanded takes its quality from the genoframe. The bill uses only genoframes of the minimum quality or better.
- Without either, any crafter may finish the implant, and one that comes out below the minimum is crafted again. The keep-in-stock floors (see [keeping stock](topic:keeping-stock)) stop this before your materials run low.

Every implant of the plan, inherited ones included, is installed and crafted at that quality or better. Implants without a quality are not affected. A new plan that extends another starts with the same minimum.
With **Give the best implants to high-priority colonists** switched on (in the surgery options on the Automation tab), quality follows colonist priority:

Implanner never replaces a healthy body part with a worse one. An awful bionic arm works worse than a natural arm, so it waits for a better item, unless the colonist's arm is missing or badly damaged. When several items qualify, the best one goes to the colonist whose turn comes first.

With Quality Bionics Remastered or Vanilla Genetics Expanded loaded, implant items come in qualities from awful to legendary, and the quality changes how well the implant works. A plan then shows a **Minimum quality** button beside **Delete plan**.

Every exchange is an extra surgery. A colonist only gets one while no other Implanner surgery is waiting for them and the concurrent surgeries limit has room. An implant is never exchanged when removing it would also take something else off the body part.
help_source.Implanner/Help/3-automation/01-how-autom: Batching delays surgery until several implants can be installed in one anesthetic sleep. A batch is everything the colonist needs next, either their current tier or their whole plan, depending on the iteration strategy (see [surgery options](topic:surgery-options)). One strategy skips batching entirely and schedules each implant as soon as it is reserved and on site.
Automation checks the colony a couple of times per in-game hour, and every edit you make triggers an immediate extra pass:
Operations wait until the colonist is fit for surgery, and colonies never take items from each other's stock: items are reserved and installed where the colonist lives.

1. Count what enlisted colonists still miss.
2. Queue crafting bills for implants the colony can build (see [production options](topic:production-options)).
3. Reserve finished items from storage for specific colonists, following priorities and tiers.
4. When everything a colonist needs next is reserved and on site, append the operations to their bill list in one block, after any bills already queued.
![The colony summary with production and surgery status](colony-next.png)

The colony summary at the top of the Overview tab shows all of this: whether automation is on, what production is crafting or waiting for, how many implants are in stock and still queued, and who is next for surgery. Hover the production or surgery figures for a breakdown per implant, including what each item is waiting for.
help_source.Implanner/Help/3-automation/02-productio: To give implant crafting a bench of its own, check **Implanner bench** on the bench's Bills tab. The checkbox appears only on benches that can craft implants. The bills already on the bench are suspended, and Implanner places its crafting bills on it before any other bench. While it is checked, you cannot add, paste, suspend or resume bills on it.
Every bill also respects the keep-in-stock floors (see [keeping stock](topic:keeping-stock)).

When several recipes make the same implant, Implanner prefers an available route it can pay for now. A free base implant can be upgraded; otherwise, a direct recipe can make the advanced implant from materials. If only the upgrade route is enabled, intermediary production can make the base first. Recipes must be researched and supported by an eligible bench.
![A fabrication bench handed over to Implanner](implanner-bench.png)

Uncheck it to take the bench back. Bills that were already suspended when you checked it stay suspended, and the rest resume. If you remove Implanner while a bench is checked, the bench keeps working, but you have to resume its bills yourself.

With **Automatically add crafting bills for missing implants** switched on, Implanner places bills for missing implants at benches that can make them, and removes its own bills when the need disappears. Bills you created yourself are never removed. Each bill runs one craft, in the order the surgeries will install them: with Full sets, a colonist's legs come before their arms if legs rank higher in the plan.

- **Benches that may hold bills** caps how many benches per colony work on implants at once. A bench holds up to two Implanner bills, so the next bill is already waiting when the first is done. Implanner benches count toward it.
- **Only allow bill creation at idle benches** keeps implant bills off benches that already have work waiting, so your own queues keep priority.
- **Only use Implanner benches** keeps implant bills on Implanner benches, so a colony without one crafts no implants. Switched off, other benches are used once every Implanner bench holds two bills.
- **Required crafting skill for production bills** keeps expensive materials away from low-skill crafters.
- **Allow production bills for missing intermediaries** follows shortfalls down the chain: one advanced component short for the next bionic leg means an advanced component bill first. While an implant waits for a raw resource such as plasteel, spare benches build the advanced components it will need. Manufactured items such as components and base implants qualify. Raw resources like steel are never crafted, even when a smelting recipe could produce them; you still have to gather them yourself.
help_source.Implanner/Help/3-automation/03-keeping-s: ![An implant reservation holding one bionic arm back](implant-reservations.png)
Two settings stop automation from draining your stockpiles.

**Implant reservations** hold finished implants back for manual use. Reserve one bionic arm and automation only assigns arms beyond the first, keeping one free for emergency surgery or trade. Production still counts a held-back item as missing, so the stock is replenished. Upgrade bills also leave held-back implants and implants needed for planned surgeries untouched. Only spare implants can be used as production ingredients.

**Keep in stock** sets resource floors for production. A crafting bill is only added when the colony can pay for it, on top of the materials its queued bills still need, and keep at least the configured amount of every ingredient. Steel at 2000 means implant crafting never drags your steel below 2000. If you spend materials and a bill nobody has started no longer fits, Implanner removes it and adds it again once the stock is back.
help_source.Implanner/Help/3-automation/04-surgery-o: **Iteration strategy** decides the order in which implants are delivered. Colonist priority on the Overview tab always decides who goes first.
**Give the best implants to high-priority colonists** appears when a mod gives implants a quality. See [minimum quality](topic:minimum-quality).

**Concurrent surgeries** caps how many colonists per colony can have operations scheduled at the same time. It starts at one per ten colonists. With **Count existing patients** on, colonists and slaves lying in medical beds or downed and awaiting treatment take up slots too, so new implant surgeries wait until the hospital has room. Prisoners, guests and patients visiting from other factions never take up a slot.

**Assign surgery bills to best available doctor** (on by default) restricts Implanner surgery bills to the most skilled doctor at each colony. The restriction follows the best doctor as colonists arrive and leave. Nobody can operate on themselves, so the best doctor's own surgeries go to the next best doctor. Switch it off to set a fixed minimum Medicine skill instead.

- **Tier batching**: every colonist gets the implants in their best tier first, then work moves down the tiers. A colonist goes into surgery once their whole tier is reserved. Each colonist needs more surgeries, but every colonist benefits sooner.
- **Full sets**: finish one colonist's whole plan before starting the next. Surgery waits until the whole plan is reserved. Each colonist needs fewer surgeries, but the last colonist in priority order waits the longest.
- **ASAP**: every implant in stock is scheduled right away for the colonist with the highest priority who is missing it. At equal priority, legs go to the slowest colonist, and arms go to colonists carrying a melee weapon first, then to whoever has the highest Crafting and Intellectual skills combined. Nothing waits for a batch: a single bionic leg is scheduled as soon as it is reserved and on site, even if that means one surgery per implant.
help_source.Implanner/Help/3-automation/05-when-auto: Switching it off first asks what to do with the bills automation already created. Checked bills are removed. Unchecked bills stay in place and are picked up again when automation is switched back on. Reserved items are released either way, and Cancel keeps automation on.

With a multi-level colony mod active (Strata, MultiFloors, As above So below), automation stands down on its own. Vanilla surgery cannot fetch an implant across a level boundary, so rather than schedule operations that can never complete, Implanner releases its reservations and leaves the work to you. Bills it already created stay in place for you to keep or cancel. Everything else keeps functioning, and implants you install by hand still count toward progress.

**Enable automation** at the top of the tab is the master switch. Switched off, Implanner becomes a planning tool only: plans, progress, and rankings keep working, but nothing is reserved, crafted, or scheduled.
help_source.Implanner/Help/4-sharing/01-exporting-pl: **Export** on the Plans tab writes all of your plans, including their implant picks and extends-links, to a small text file or the clipboard.
Exports carry no colonists, assignments, or save data, only the plans, so they work in any save and any colony. Implants from mods are tagged with the mod they came from.

- **Save** writes an .xml file to the Implanner folder (or Desktop, home folder, or a folder you choose).
- **Copy to clipboard** puts the same text on the clipboard, ready to paste into a chat message or forum post.
help_source.Implanner/Help/4-sharing/02-importing-pl: **Import** on the Plans tab reads a plans export from a file or the clipboard and shows a preview before anything happens.

- Imported plans are **added** next to your existing ones; nothing is replaced. A name that is already taken gets a number.
- Implants from mods you do not have are skipped; the rest of the plan is imported.
- A broken or unrelated file is rejected with a message and changes nothing.
Import a set at the start of every colony instead of rebuilding your favorite plans by hand.
help_source.Implanner/Help/5-mods/01-how-modded-impl: Implanner does not need a list of supported mods to read implants. It reads every surgery the game has loaded, from vanilla, the expansions and every mod, and any surgery that installs an implant on a body part becomes an entry in the picker. The same data tells Implanner which implants can share a body:

- **One replacement per part**: a bionic arm swaps the shoulder out, so two replacements never share a part, and a replacement clears every implant mounted on it or on the parts below it.
- **Implants on one part**: they coexist unless the surgery marks them as incompatible. This is how skin glands exclude each other in the base game, and how mods mark module slots.
- **Removal on install**: some implants remove a rival anywhere on the body the moment they go in. Two implants that remove each other can never coexist.
- **Surgeries that clear a body part**: some surgeries remove everything on a body part before adding an implant that does not replace it. Implants installed afterwards stay, so Implanner installs such an implant first and puts back anything it pushes out.
- **Modules that mount on bionics**: a surgery whose worker is written to install onto an artificial part shares that part with the bionic instead of replacing it.
- **Upgrades in place**: a surgery that removes one implant and adds another upgrades the installed part. The upgraded version is listed as its own implant.
- **Purchase-only items**: an implant whose item no workbench can craft is hidden until the matching option on the Options tab is switched on.

Two things cannot be read. Modules that a colonist inserts from the inventory without any surgery are never listed, and rules that exist only in a mod's code, with nothing in its data, cannot be seen. Everything a mod expresses through its surgeries works without any change to Implanner.
**Bionic modularity**: every module occupies a slot on its body part, so one combat module and one work module fit on the same arm while two combat modules do not. Modules for limbs install onto a bionic limb and share the part with it, so a planned bionic arm and a planned arm module coexist. Ticking a limb module while the plan has no bionic on that part opens a prompt that lists the bionics able to host it, with the least advanced host selected by default. **Add to plan** adds your choice and the module together. **Cancel** adds nothing.
**Vanilla Genetics Expanded**: its hybrid implants for colonists are listed with the other implants. Its animal implants are not, since Implanner plans colonists only.

Every implant mod that uses the game's surgery data works without any setup. Players have confirmed Expanded Prosthetics and Organ Engineering and CeleTech, whose implants are read exactly like vanilla content. The mods below were checked one by one against their data.
![The plain and advanced bionic eye rows showing an overrides caption naming the picked modular bionic eye](modular-eye.png)
![The plan after Add to plan: the bionic leg and the module are both picked](requirement-added.png)

**Quality Bionics Remastered**: bionics come in qualities, and a better bionic works better and has more hit points. The implant tooltip shows the part efficiency from awful to legendary, and each plan sets the lowest quality it installs (see [minimum quality](topic:minimum-quality)).
**Elite Bionics Framework**: implants that raise or lower a body part's hit points show the change in their tooltip.

**[FSF] Advanced Bionics Expansion**: mechanite strains exclude each other. Injecting one strain removes any other strain in the body, so the picker treats every strain as one slot and the overrides caption names the strain being replaced. Immunity-enhancing mechanites are not a strain and coexist with every strain. Its advanced bionic bladder and advanced hygiene enhancer are covered by the mod compatibility options together with Dubs Bad Hygiene.

Some hybrid implants replace a body part: the hibernation module replaces the brain. Others sit on the body part: neuron reinforcement sits on the brain. Regular implants can go on a body part that has a hybrid implant sitting on it, but not on one that has been replaced.
![The other strain rows showing an overrides caption naming the picked strain](mechanites-overrides.png)

**Dubs Bad Hygiene**: the bionic bladder and the hygiene enhancer are torso implants that the game lets a colonist combine with the advanced versions from [FSF] Advanced Bionics Expansion. The two mod compatibility options decide whether Implanner allows that as well.

- Implanner installs the hybrid implant first, so nothing needs to come out.
- If the colonist already has implants there, Implanner lets them drop out, holds them for that colonist, and installs them again right after.
- Implanner never installs a hybrid implant while something on that body part would be lost for good.
Hybrid implants take their quality from the genoframe they are made with (see [minimum quality](topic:minimum-quality)).
![The requirement prompt for a leg module](requirement-prompt.png)
Installing any hybrid implant pushes out everything already installed on that body part. The pushed-out implants drop next to the doctor.

**Integrated Implants**: extra arms allow one per side, and picking a second kind of extra arm on the same side overrides the first. Subdermal armour and its prestige version, the shoulder turrets, the tails and the implanted explosives each form a group where only one can be installed. The modular bionics are upgrades in place: pick a modular bionic eye and automation installs a bionic eye first if the colonist has none, then the upgrade surgery, which consumes one component and no second bionic eye. These upgrades need EBSG Framework and are not offered while Medical System Expansion 2 is loaded. The modules themselves are inserted from the inventory without any surgery, so they are not listed.
![A picked mechanite strain in the Torso list](mechanites-picked.png)
help_source.Implanner/Help/5-mods/03-mod-options.md#: The Options tab holds plan compatibility settings and the skill-slider display range. Automation settings live on the Automation tab. Plan and automation settings are shared by everyone in a multiplayer game.
![Hovering the option shows the affected implants](options-purchase-tip.png)
![Hovering an option lists the implants it affects and their mods](options-bladder-tip.png)

- Picking one version in a plan overrides the other, with the usual caption in the picker.
- A colonist who already has either version counts as done for that slot, so automation never installs the second one.
- A colonist who already carries both keeps both. Nothing is ever removed.
- Picks made while the option was on stay stored and return when it is switched back on.

**Allow multiple bladder implants** and **Allow multiple hygiene enhancers** are on by default, which matches the game: a colonist can carry the version from Dubs Bad Hygiene and the version from [FSF] Advanced Bionics Expansion at the same time, and their effects stack. Switch one off to treat that pair as one slot:
![The Options tab with the Mod compatibility and Catalog sections](options-tab.png)

**Show purchase-only implants** is off by default. Switched on, it lists implants whose item no workbench can craft, such as archotech parts, which only arrive through trade, quests or salvage. The tooltip names every affected implant that is loaded.
Each tooltip lists the affected implants that are loaded and the mod each one comes from.
![The Limbs picker listing archotech legs and arms](picker-purchase-only.png)

**Maximum skill slider value** sets the upper end of the Medical and Crafting sliders, from 20 to 100 in steps of 10. The default is 20. Increase it to choose higher minimum skills when using a mod such as Endless Growth. This is a personal display preference: changing it leaves existing minimums, automatic doctor selection and bill eligibility unchanged.

With the option on, the picker shows them like any other implant. A planned purchase-only implant never holds anything else back: the rest of the batch goes ahead without it, and once its item is in stock it is installed with the colonist's next batch, or right away under ASAP. Switching the option off hides the rows again and removes these implants from the Implant reservations menu, but picks already made stay in the plan and keep working. A mod that adds a crafting recipe for the item makes the implant an ordinary one automatically, regardless of this option.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/1-basics/01-quality-job: New quality bills are managed by default. New buildings are opt-in unless you enable **{k:QJ_SettingsManageNewConstruction}**. When adding the mod to a save, the existing-bills prompt lets you keep their current behavior or enable automatic selection of the best finisher.

- For gear and art, open a workbench bill's **Details** and use its **{k:QJ_QualityPanelTitle}** panel.
- For a new building with quality, select its blueprint or frame and use **{k:QJ_GizmoQualityJobLabel}**.
- To improve existing furniture, select it, choose a target in **{k:QJ_GizmoQualityJobLabel}**, then click **{k:QJ_StartRebuilding}**.
Start with [sharing unfinished work](topic:sharing-work), [choosing finishers](topic:finishers), or [setting up a bill](topic:quality-bills).

Quality Jobs lets your colony share the work while a qualified worker does the finishing touch. Colonists, colony mechs and supported robots can finish work they are capable of doing. In RimWorld, the **finisher** determines quality. The mod chooses who finishes; the result is still a normal quality roll.

Click the Quality Jobs icon beside the view toggles in the lower right. **{k:QJ_TabOptions}** holds your defaults; **{k:QJ_TabHelp}** explains the controls. Choose a chapter above and a topic on the left.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/1-basics/02-sharing-wor: An idle item is released from its original worker and bill so a compatible bill can pick it up. While that bill's unfinished item is waiting or being hauled, it does not start a duplicate. Active work is not interrupted just to hand it to someone else.

The next worker needs a usable bill for the same recipe. The item's ingredients must be allowed by that bill, and its style must match. The item must also be reachable, allowed and available to reserve. Sharing does not bypass ordinary work assignments or bill restrictions.

Turn sharing off to return shared work to ordinary ownership. Managed bills can still reserve their final touch. Turning off **{k:QJ_ManageBill}** releases that bill's quality-waiting work; it does not turn off sharing for the colony.

Sharing early work is different from reserving the final touch. A managed item paused just before completion shows **Author: reserved (Quality Jobs)**. It waits for a [qualifying finisher](topic:finishers); an ordinary worker cannot finish it through sharing.

When **{k:QJ_SettingsAllowRobotPreparation}** is off, a shared unfinished item remains reserved for colonist work while its original bill still exists and is managed. Picking it up through an unmanaged bill does not let a mech or robot take over that work. Eligible mechs and robots can still perform finishing assignments from Quality Jobs.

With **{k:QJ_SettingsShareWork}** enabled in Options, an idle unfinished item can be continued by another eligible worker, even if its original crafter has died. Sharing works independently of **{k:QJ_ManageBill}**.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/1-basics/03-finishers.m: Otherwise eligible workers remain in the comparison while away, downed, asleep, mentally broken or recharging, including robots docked in their stations. If no top-ranked worker can finish on this map, the work waits. For example, a better crafter away in a caravan can prevent a lower-ranked worker at home from finishing. There is no timeout that lowers the quality requirement.

Auto-adjust compares eligible colonists, colony mechs and supported robots and chooses the worker with the highest expected quality. Skill, Inspired Creativity, production-specialist bonuses and supported mod quality bonuses all count. This maximizes average quality; it does not guarantee the result of an individual roll.

- **Finisher skill** sets a minimum skill level.
- **{k:QJ_AutoBest}** chooses the best eligible worker automatically. The manual slider is kept for when you turn this off.
- **{k:QJ_RequireInspired}** waits for that inspiration. Completing the work consumes it as usual.
- **{k:QJ_RequireSpecialist}** requires an Ideology role that grants a production quality bonus. This option appears with Ideology.
With Auto-adjust off, any capable worker meeting your manual skill threshold and other requirements can finish. A better worker elsewhere in the colony does not block them.

**{k:QJ_OddsHeader}** compares your **{k:QJ_OddsColConfig}** with the current **{k:QJ_OddsColBest}** candidate. These are chances, not promises. **Eligible finishers** lists workers who can qualify on this map now; away, downed or mentally broken workers are excluded from that list.

**{k:QJ_SettingsHighPriorityFinish}** makes assigned finishing work come before other work except firefighting, medical care, rescue and bed rest. It does not interrupt the current job. With it off, finishing comes first within its work type, after any higher-ranked work types. The worker must be able to perform the item's normal work type.
Use these controls on a bill or a building. Other eligible workers may do the earlier work; only the finishing touch must meet your requirements.

Mechs and supported robots must meet the same finisher requirements as colonists. Requiring Inspired Creativity or a production-specialist role still excludes workers without it. Turning off **{k:QJ_SettingsAllowRobotPreparation}** reserves the earlier work for colonists; eligible mechs and robots can still take Quality Jobs finishing assignments.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/2-crafting/01-quality-b: ![A workbench bill with its Quality Jobs panel](crafting-bill.png)
Clear **{k:QJ_ManageBill}** to let it complete normally again. Its shared work can still be continued by other workers when sharing is enabled.

When a finisher qualifies, Quality Jobs creates a temporary **Finish …** bill assigned to them. They collect the unfinished item and complete it. The temporary bill removes itself afterward. Waiting items can be hauled and stored like other unfinished items.

The original bill's maximum skill level and specific worker assignment apply until the item is set aside for finishing. You can assign the work to a trainee while a more skilled colonist, colony mech or supported robot takes the dedicated finishing bill. Finishers must still be capable of the recipe and meet the Quality Jobs requirements.

Open **Details** on a bill for a quality item. The **{k:QJ_QualityPanelTitle}** panel appears beside the normal bill controls for supported recipes that leave an unfinished item. Recipes without quality or unfinished work keep their normal behavior.

Enable **{k:QJ_ManageBill}**, then choose the [finisher requirements](topic:finishers). Ordinary workers can do most of the crafting. If the current worker qualifies, they finish directly; otherwise the nearly finished item is set aside, and the bill can start more items within its stock cap.

The **{k:QJ_StatusHeader}** section shows shared **Unfinished** work, items **Waiting** for a finisher, and items already assigned for **Finishing**. Hover the status and finisher list for more detail. See [when work waits](topic:waiting) if nothing is progressing.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/2-crafting/02-targets-a: At the cap, managed bills stop starting new items. Resuming or finishing existing items is still allowed, so the queue can drain. If no finisher qualifies, lowering the requirements or restoring an eligible worker can unblock the queue.

This retry behavior applies to **Do X times**. For **Do until you have X**, use the normal bill's quality range to decide what counts toward the stock target. **Do forever** continues as usual. A quality target does not itself choose a better finisher; set the finisher requirements too.

**Stock cap** limits new work on a product on this map. Its unfinished items count together across bills and benches, but only managed bills enforce the cap. **0 means unlimited.** Finished items in storage do not count.

**{k:QJ_MinQualityLabel}** asks a fixed-count bill to keep trying until it produces enough items at that quality or better. A below-target item is kept, but does not use up one of the bill's remaining repetitions. Each extra attempt uses more materials. **{k:QJ_AnyQuality}** accepts every result.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/3-construction/01-new-b: ![Quality Job controls for a new building](construction.png)

The normal **Build copy** command carries a managed blueprint or frame's Quality Jobs settings to the new blueprints. To manage all new quality buildings automatically, enable **{k:QJ_SettingsManageNewConstruction}** in Options.

Select a blueprint or frame for a building with quality, such as a bed or chair. **Left-click Quality Job** to toggle management using your construction defaults. **Right-click** it to choose the finisher requirements and target quality.

Managed construction has a sparkle overlay. Builders can do the early work, but a frame waits at the end until a qualifying builder can finish. If the current builder already qualifies, construction finishes without a handoff.
Leave **{k:QJ_MinQualityLabel}** at **{k:QJ_NoRetries}** to accept the first result. Choose a quality to [rebuild below-target results](topic:retries).
Changing a setting in this panel enables management. **{k:QJ_Clear}** removes it and lets the build finish normally. Select several eligible blueprints or frames to apply a change to all of them.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/3-construction/02-retri: Retries use labor and materials, and some materials are lost each time. The building is unavailable while it is being replaced. Good finisher requirements reduce wasted attempts; a very ambitious target can take many tries.

A building below its **{k:QJ_MinQualityLabel}** is marked for deconstruction, then rebuilt at the same place. This repeats until it reaches the target or you stop management. **{k:QJ_NoRetries}** keeps the first result while still applying your finisher requirements.

Replacements keep material, orientation, style and paint. Beds also keep medical and prisoner settings. Original bed owners return when the loop ends if they are still eligible and have not taken another bed. Other mods' custom building settings follow their usual deconstruct-and-rebuild behavior.

Use **{k:QJ_Clear}**, toggle off **{k:QJ_GizmoQualityJobLabel}**, or cancel the deconstruction order to stop the loop. If the original has already been demolished, Clear lets the replacement finish normally while retaining its saved settings.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/3-construction/03-exist: Starting uses the same [deconstruct-and-rebuild loop](topic:retries) as new construction. Plan for the material cost and temporary loss of beds or furniture. Clear management or cancel deconstruction if you change your mind.

Buildings already meeting the target are kept. A building must be available to construct and free of other deconstruction or reinstall orders. If none of the selected buildings need an eligible upgrade, the panel tells you so.

Select one or more completed quality buildings and click **{k:QJ_GizmoQualityJobLabel}**. Choose a target quality and builder requirements, then click **{k:QJ_StartRebuilding}**. Opening the panel or changing its settings alone does not demolish anything.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/4-options/01-defaults.m: **{k:QJ_SettingsBillDefaults}** control bills that follow the defaults. Individual bill settings override them. Changing a bill default can therefore affect existing bills that have not been customized. The unfinished stock cap is shared by product, rather than separately for every bill.

**{k:QJ_SettingsConstructionDefaults}** are applied when a build is enabled or automatically managed. Existing managed buildings keep their own settings. The construction target uses **{k:QJ_NoRetries}**; the crafting target uses **{k:QJ_AnyQuality}**.

**{k:QJ_SettingsShareWork}** and **{k:QJ_SettingsHighPriorityFinish}** apply across the colony. See [sharing](topic:sharing-work) and [finishers](topic:finishers) for their effects. **{k:QJ_DisableButton}** is intended for [safe removal](topic:removing), not for pausing one bill.
![The Options tab with bill and construction defaults](options.png)

**{k:QJ_SettingsAllowRobotPreparation}** is saved for the current colony and starts enabled, including in existing saves. Turn it off to reserve work on managed crafting bills and construction plans for colonists, so they receive the work's skill experience. This also stops mechs and robots already doing that work. Eligible mechs and supported robots can still finish jobs assigned by Quality Jobs. Ordinary unmanaged jobs are unaffected; [shared unfinished items](topic:sharing-work) keep the original managed bill's restriction. This option is available with a save loaded and is synchronized in Multiplayer.

With a save loaded, Options changes that colony's settings. From the main menu, the mod settings supply defaults for new saves. **{k:QJ_SettingsShowToolbarButton}** is your personal display preference; hiding it does not disable the mod. You can still open the mod settings from the game's Options menu.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/4-options/02-waiting.md: Start with **{k:QJ_StatusHeader}** in the bill or construction panel. **No eligible finisher** means the work is waiting for your requirements to be met, not that its progress was lost.

- Is the required work type enabled for the intended finisher, and are they on this map and able to work?
- Is the skill requirement too high, or are you waiting for Inspired Creativity or a production specialist?
- Is Auto-adjust waiting for a worker with higher expected quality to become available, for example to return from a caravan or finish recharging?
- Can the worker reach and reserve the item or frame, and use the bench? Check forbidden items, allowed areas, bill restrictions and competing reservations.
- Is the stock cap full? Finish waiting items before starting more, or deliberately raise the cap.

Most setting changes apply immediately, even while paused. Some changing pawn facts and optional-mod bonuses refresh after simulation advances; if a recent change is not reflected yet, resume briefly. High-priority finishing waits until the pawn next looks for work.

**This bill's unfinished item is waiting to be resumed** prevents a duplicate while shared work is already waiting or being hauled. Let that item become available rather than supplying another set of ingredients.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/4-options/03-other-mods: Avoid overlapping unfinished-work managers. The welcome notice identifies detected conflicts, including **No Job Authors** and **Finish it!**. They can bypass reserved work or expect an unfinished item to remain attached to its original bill. Turning sharing off does not remove every conflict.

**Vanilla Skills Expanded:** construction, crafting and art quality bonuses count in finisher selection and the odds preview. Speed bonuses do not give a quality preference. Changes to these bonuses may need a little simulation time to appear.
**Implanner** can request quality-managed implant bills. **WorkRoles** can organize the finishing work through work assignments; the finished item's work type must still be enabled for the pawn.

**Quality Bionics Remastered:** supported quality-producing recipes can use the bill panel. **Vanilla Genetics Expanded:** recipes whose quality comes from a genoframe keep that ingredient's quality rules; choosing a finisher cannot improve the ingredient's quality.
Colony settings and quality-work commands are synchronized in Multiplayer. Toolbar visibility and which help topics you have read are personal preferences.
Quality Jobs requires Harmony and supports RimWorld 1.6 and 1.7. No DLC is required. Ideology adds the production-specialist requirement; ordinary quality management works without it.

**Biotech mechs, Misc. Robots and Misc. Robots++:** colony-controlled workers that can perform the required work can qualify as finishers. Robots keep their own work capabilities; a hauling or cleaning robot cannot finish crafting or construction. **{k:QJ_SettingsAllowRobotPreparation}** controls whether mechs and supported robots may also do the earlier work on managed jobs. Turning it off keeps them available for finishing.
help_source.QualityJobs/Help/4-options/04-removing.m: Disabling restores set-aside items to vanilla ownership and discards the save's bill conditions, construction plans and stock caps. Removing the mod without disabling first can leave unfinished items without an owner; those items must be cancelled.

For just one bill, clear **{k:QJ_ManageBill}**. For a construction plan, use **{k:QJ_Clear}** or toggle **{k:QJ_GizmoQualityJobLabel}** off. Use the global Disable button only when you want to discard Quality Jobs configuration for the whole save.
If you keep Quality Jobs installed, loading the save activates it again with default settings. Disabling is a preparation for removal, not a lasting per-save off switch.

1. Let replacement buildings finish first, so their saved bed settings and paint are restored.
2. Open Options and click **{k:QJ_DisableButton}**, then confirm.
3. Save the game. Remove the mod before loading that save again.
help_source.Readouts/Help/1-basics/01-what-readouts-: Readouts replaces the resource readout in the top left corner of the screen with groups of resources that you arrange yourself:
The gear button at the top of the panel opens the editor, where you build groups and set options (see [The editor window](topic:the-editor-window)).

Each group is a band with a colored stripe. A band shows resource icons with their counts, and a group can hold up to three tiers of resources that you reveal when you need them (see [Showing more tiers](topic:showing-more-tiers)).
help_source.Readouts/Help/1-basics/02-reading-a-band:
- The colored stripe identifies the group. The six colors follow the order of the groups you have turned on and repeat after that, so hiding a group shifts the colors of the bands below it.
- The triangles, one per tier the group has. A white triangle marks a tier that is shown, a dim one a tier that is hidden.
- One icon and counter per resource or resource pool (see [What a resource pool is](topic:what-a-resource-pool-is)).
Each group you have turned on is one band in the panel. From left to right, a band shows the colored stripe, the triangles, and one icon with a counter per resource or resource pool:
Counts above ten thousand are shortened, so 12,800 reads 12.8k. The tooltip shows the exact number (see [Hovering and clicking a slot](topic:hovering-and-clicking-a-slot)).

A counter changes color when the count falls to a limit you set for that resource (see [Slot options](topic:slot-options)). It also turns orange when it shows a negative number, which happens when your bills and blueprints need more than you have (see [Planned work](topic:planned-work)).
help_source.Readouts/Help/1-basics/03-showing-more-t: A group can hold up to three tiers. The first tier is always shown; the others stay hidden until you reveal them. The Food group with only its first tier:
Click the stripe or the triangles to reveal the next tier. Each click adds one tier, and a click on the last tier goes back to the first. Hovering the stripe shows a tooltip that says so:

With the vertical layout the extra tiers go below the first one instead (see [Tier layout](topic:tier-layout)). Hovering a band can also reveal its tiers for as long as the mouse stays on it (see [Hover options](topic:hover-options)).
Which tiers you have open is your own view. Other players in a multiplayer game keep theirs.
One click adds the second tier to the right of the first, and another click adds the third:
help_source.Readouts/Help/1-basics/04-hovering-and-c: Click an icon or its counter to select the matching stacks on the map. Hold Shift to add them to the current selection, or to deselect them when they are all selected already. The selection follows the count options on the Options tab (see [Count options](topic:count-options)) and stops at the game's limit of 200 selected items.

Hold the mouse over an icon to see the name, the exact count, and the description behind the counter. For a resource pool (see [What a resource pool is](topic:what-a-resource-pool-is)) the tooltip lists every member you own some of, with its own count:
With the click option "Jump camera to clicked resource" the camera also moves to the closest of the stacks the click selected (see [Click options](topic:click-options)).
help_source.Readouts/Help/1-basics/05-searching.md#b: Search options let you hide zero-count results or remove the field from the header (see [Search options](topic:search-options)). The counts follow the count options on the Options tab (see [Count options](topic:count-options)).

Matching resources appear in a Results section above the groups, with up to three rows and a line that says how many more there are. Resources with a count other than zero come first, in alphabetical order, and resources with a count of zero follow when the search options allow them. Slots in your groups that match are highlighted as well; a pool slot matches by its pool name. Click the X next to the field, or press Escape while typing, to clear the search.
Type in the search field at the top of the panel to find any resource, whether it sits in a group or not:
help_source.Readouts/Help/1-basics/06-the-editor-win: ![The Overview tab with the Food group selected](editor-window.png)

The four buttons at the top are Import, Export, Set defaults, and Restore defaults. Import and Export share a setup, Set defaults saves a personal setup for future colonies, and Restore defaults resets the current colony (see [Sharing groups](topic:sharing-groups) and [New-game defaults](topic:new-game-defaults)).

You can also open the Options tab through Options → Mod Options → EPrime's Readouts, including from the main menu. Both routes use the same settings window (see [Panel position and size](topic:panel-position-and-size)).

- The tabs at the top switch between Overview, Options, and Help. Options holds the panel's display, counting, position and size settings, and Help is this manual.
- The Groups panel on the left lists your groups and selects the one you edit (see [The groups list](topic:the-groups-list)).
- The middle panel is the Group Editor for the selected group. The two buttons at its top switch it to the Resource Pool Editor (see [Tiers in the Group Editor](topic:tiers-in-the-group-editor) and [Editing a pool](topic:editing-a-pool)).
- The Resources panel on the right lists everything you can add to a group or a pool (see [The Resources panel](topic:the-resources-panel)).
- The Help row at the top of each panel folds a short description in or out.
The editor can stay open while the game runs, and every change applies at once. There is no Apply or Cancel button.
Click the gear button at the top left of the readout panel to open the editor. The Overview tab is where you build groups and pools:
help_source.Readouts/Help/2-groups/01-the-groups-lis: The group name and a rename button sit above the tiers in the Group Editor.

- Click a name to open the group in the Group Editor.
- Click the checkmark to show or hide the group in the readout. This is your own view; other players in a multiplayer game keep theirs.
- Click the X to delete the group. A confirmation prompt appears first.
- Drag a name up or down to change the order of the bands.
- Type a name in the field at the bottom and click Add to create a group. The new group opens in the Group Editor and is turned on for you.
The Groups panel lists every group in the order the readout shows them:
help_source.Readouts/Help/2-groups/02-tiers-in-the-g: The tiers belong to the save, so every player in a multiplayer game sees the same groups.
A group starts with one tier, and a new empty tier appears below as soon as the tier above it holds something. Each tier holds up to eight slots, and a resource can appear only once per group.

- Click a resource in the Resources panel to append it to the last tier, or to a new tier when that one is full.
- Drag a resource from the Resources panel onto a slot to place it there.
- Drag a slot to move it within a tier or to another tier.
- Right-click a slot to remove it from the group. A tier that ends up empty disappears, and the tiers below it move up.
- Click a slot to open its options (see [Slot options](topic:slot-options)).
![The Food group in the Group Editor](group-tiers.png)
The Group Editor shows one band per tier, with the same icons and counts as the readout:
help_source.Readouts/Help/2-groups/03-the-resources-: The Resources panel on the right lists everything you can put in a group, sorted into the game's own categories. Three filters at its top narrow the list:
A green checkmark marks an entry that is already in the selected group. Click the checkmark, or right-click the entry, to remove it from the group:
![The filters at the top of the Resources panel](resources-filters.png)
The filters are shared with the Resource Pool Editor and reset when the editor window closes. The item filter opens as a menu:
A search shows the categories and pools it matched together with the matching resources:
![The Foods category with items that are already in the group](resources-tree.png)
![A search that matched a category and a pool](resources-search.png)

- The search filter matches resource names and category names. A matching category shows all of its contents.
- The item filter switches between Resources, the items the game's own readout shows, and All Storable Items, which adds everything that can sit in a stockpile.
- The source filter limits the list to one mod, or to the base game and its expansions under Vanilla.
help_source.Readouts/Help/2-groups/04-slot-options.m:
- Show when zero keeps the slot visible when the count is zero. Turn it off and the slot disappears until you own some again. A slot with a threshold, or with a negative count, always stays visible.
- Low and Critical set the thresholds that color the counter. Enter the numbers and click Set; Clear removes them. The counter turns pale yellow at or below Low and orange at or below Critical, so Critical should be the smaller number.
- The two rows at the bottom override the count options for this resource or pool. Default follows the Options tab, while Always On and Always Off ignore it (see [Count options](topic:count-options)).

Thresholds and count overrides belong to the resource or pool, so the same resource shows the same colors and counts in every group. They are saved with the game and apply to every player. Show when zero belongs to the slot.
Click a slot in the Group Editor to open the options for that resource or resource pool (see [What a resource pool is](topic:what-a-resource-pool-is)). The options for the Meals slot:
help_source.Readouts/Help/2-groups/05-sharing-groups: Every category present in the file can be selected. You can change related categories one at a time, even if an intermediate choice is incomplete. Import stays disabled until the chosen setup has valid pool and group references; hover the disabled button to see what is missing.
Categories absent from an older export stay unchanged. Entries requiring unavailable mod content are skipped.
![Import, Export, Set defaults and Restore defaults](editor-buttons.png)

Import reads a saved file or the clipboard and shows a preview before changing anything. Select the categories you want to replace. The Player settings and enabled groups checkbox starts unchecked, so you can keep your own display preferences.

Set defaults saves a personal setup for future colonies (see [New-game defaults](topic:new-game-defaults)). Restore defaults asks for confirmation, then replaces the current colony's setup with the one shipped with Readouts. In multiplayer, that reset affects everyone's shared setup.
In multiplayer, imported groups, pools, thresholds and count overrides change the setup for everyone. Imported player settings affect only you.
The four buttons at the top of the editor share, save or reset your setup:
Export saves your groups, resource pools, thresholds, count overrides and player settings. Choose a location and file name, then click Save, or use Copy to Clipboard.
Player settings include enabled groups and your global display and counting options. Current tier depth, search text, scroll positions and temporary editor state are excluded.
help_source.Readouts/Help/2-groups/06-new-game-defau: Set defaults, at the top of the editor, lets you save this colony's setup as your personal starting point. Click Use this setup for new games to save it.
## Keep the default up to date

Current tier depth, search text, scroll positions and temporary editor state are excluded. If a mod is missing, its entries are skipped in the new colony but kept in your personal default, ready for when that content returns.
Loading a colony alone does not change your default or show this prompt. None of these choices replaces the current colony's setup.
Open Set defaults and choose Use built-in defaults for new games to remove your personal default and turn off automatic updates. Future colonies then start with the setup shipped with Readouts.
With automatic updates on, a loaded colony may have a different setup from your saved default. The first time you open the editor in that session, Readouts asks what to do:
![Saving a personal setup with automatic updates enabled](default-settings.png)
To reset the current colony instead, use Restore defaults (see [Sharing groups](topic:sharing-groups)).

Automatically update after configuration edits is optional. Turn it on before saving to keep your personal default in step with later configuration changes. Updates are saved when you close the editor or leave the game. Showing more or fewer tiers in the readout does not update the default.

- Use this setup for new games replaces your default with this colony's setup and keeps automatic updates on.
- Keep my default for this session leaves the saved default unchanged while you edit this colony during the session.
- Turn off auto-update keeps your saved default and disables automatic updates.
![The choices when a colony differs from the personal default](default-conflict.png)
Future colonies receive its groups, pools, thresholds, count overrides and enabled groups. Your current global display and counting options stay in use. Existing colonies keep their own setups.
help_source.Readouts/Help/3-pools/01-what-a-resource: A resource pool is one slot that shows the combined count of several resources. Meats, Meals, and Leathers are typical pools, with one number for the whole category instead of a slot per kind. The pools that ship with the mod, as listed in the Resource Pool Editor:

A pool uses the icon of its first member until you choose another one (see [Editing a pool](topic:editing-a-pool)). Hovering a pool slot in the readout lists the members you own some of, each with its own count (see [Hovering and clicking a slot](topic:hovering-and-clicking-a-slot)). A pool with no members shows nothing in the readout.
Pool names must be unique. Pools belong to the save, so every player in a multiplayer game sees the same pools.
![The pool list in the Resource Pool Editor](pool-list.png)
![Members of the Meals pool in the Resources panel](pool-members.png)
Click Add at the bottom and enter a name to create a pool, then click a pool in the list to edit it. The two buttons on a row rename or delete the pool.

Click the checkbox of a category to include everything in it, or the checkbox of single resources. A category with only some of its members in the pool shows a partial mark, and clicking a category name opens or closes it. A category checkbox only changes the resources currently listed under it, so an active search, item, or source filter limits what it adds or removes.
Switch the middle panel to the Resource Pool Editor with the button at its top:
Click the icon of any resource in the list to make it the pool's icon. The name of the resource you chose as the icon is shown in yellow; the automatic first-member icon is not marked.
With a pool selected, the Resources panel shows a checkbox in front of every category and resource:
help_source.Readouts/Help/3-pools/03-pools-in-groups: Deleting a pool removes its slot from every group that used it, together with its thresholds and count overrides.

In the Group Editor, pools sit under the Resource Pools branch at the top of the Resources panel. Add one to a group the same way as a resource: click it, or drag it onto a slot (see [Tiers in the Group Editor](topic:tiers-in-the-group-editor)). A search for "meal" finds the Meals pool under that branch, already in the group:

A pool slot behaves like any other slot. It can have thresholds, hide itself at zero, and override the count options (see [Slot options](topic:slot-options)). The pool's own count override applies to all of its members; overrides set on a member for its own slot do not reach into the pool.
![The Resource Pools branch with the Meals pool in the group](resources-search.png)
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/01-tier-layout.m: Tier layout decides where a group puts its extra tiers when you reveal them, whether by clicking the stripe or by hovering. Horizontal adds the tiers to the right, on the same row:
Vertical gives each tier its own row and makes the band taller:
Everything on the Options tab is your own setting. It applies to all your saves and never changes what other players see.
![Horizontal layout: the Drugs group with two tiers](tiers-horizontal.png)
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/02-hover-options: A hovered band shows the tiers you opened, never more:
![The hovered Food group: the first tier is yours, the other two came from hovering](hover-expanded.png)
Collapse when not hovering appears once Expand on hover is on, and hides instead of reveals. Every band shrinks to its stripe and triangles until you hover it:
![The hovered Drugs band with its two tiers](collapse-hover.png)
Expand on hover reveals every tier of a band while the mouse is over it. Tiers added by hovering show yellow triangles, so you can still see which tiers you opened yourself:
Both options follow the tier layout you chose (see [Tier layout](topic:tier-layout)).
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/03-count-options: Ignore forbidden items leaves forbidden stacks out of the count.

Because carried items are not counted, the counter normally drops the moment a colonist picks up a stack. Material for a blueprint is the exception. With Reserve resources for buildables turned on (see [Planned work](topic:planned-work)), the counter already subtracted what the blueprint needs when you placed it, so picking that material up and delivering it does not lower the counter a second time.
Some items are never counted: rotten items, items in parts of the map you have not explored yet, and items a colonist is carrying or keeps in an inventory or a container.
Only count items in storage counts stacks in stockpile zones and in storage buildings such as shelves. Loose items lying around the map are left out:
With the option off, everything on the map counts:
Count options decide which stacks are counted in every counter the panel shows. Both are on when you install the mod.

The panel refreshes its counts every few seconds of game time. Changing a count option refreshes them at once, even while the game is paused. A resource or pool can override both options for every slot that shows it (see [Slot options](topic:slot-options)).
![The same slots with storage only off](storage-only-off.png)
With the option off, the same slots stop at zero:
Planned work options subtract material that bills or blueprints have already claimed.
With Show overruns as negative numbers on, a counter that planned work pushes below zero shows the shortfall in orange:
![The same slots with negative numbers off](negatives-off.png)

- Reserve resources for bill items subtracts the ingredients your outstanding bills still have to consume. A bill reserves an ingredient only when there is exactly one way to satisfy that requirement. "Any leather" and similar open choices reserve nothing. A "do X times" bill reserves X runs, a "do until you have X" bill reserves the runs needed to reach the target, and a "do forever" bill reserves one run. Suspended bills reserve nothing.
- Reserve resources for buildables subtracts the materials your blueprints and part-built frames still need. Material already delivered to a frame, or picked up by a colonist to deliver, counts as spent and is not subtracted a second time. Forbidden blueprints are ignored.
- Show overruns as negative numbers displays how far short you are when planned work needs more than you have, instead of stopping at zero.
- Quality Jobs support estimates how many attempts a quality target will take and reserves for all of them. The row is greyed out when EPrime's Quality Jobs is not installed or too old, and the reason shows on hover.
Planned work is rescanned about every seventeen seconds of game time, so a new bill can take that long to show in the counts.
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/05-search-option: ![The header with the mod name instead](header-modname.png)

Hide zero-count results drops resources with a count of zero from the search results. While Only count items in storage is on, resources with nothing in storage never appear in the results, whatever this option says (see [Count options](topic:count-options)).

Turn it off for a plain header; any search that was active is cleared at the same time. Show mod name appears once the field is hidden, and decides whether the header shows the mod name or nothing at all:
Show search filter puts the search field in the panel header:
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/06-click-options: Jump camera to clicked resource moves the camera to the closest of the stacks the click selected when you click a slot in the readout. With the option off, clicking still selects the stacks but the camera stays where it is.
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/07-panel-positio: The sliders under Position and Size Options adjust the panel:
Use vanilla readout, at the bottom of Display Options, asks for confirmation before switching to the game's readout and its categorized-readout toggle. You can keep Readouts installed.

- Horizontal offset and Vertical offset move the panel away from the corner, from 0 to 200 pixels. Both start at 7.
- Panel width sets the width of the header and of the search results, from 80 to 400 pixels with 140 as the default. Wide bands extend past it, and a wider panel fits more search-result columns, up to six.
- Bottom margin keeps the panel clear of the bottom of the screen, from 0 to 500 pixels with 200 as the default. A panel that would reach past it scrolls with the mouse wheel instead.
Changes preview immediately. Reset position and size restores these four defaults without changing your other options.
To bring Readouts back after closing the settings window, open Options → Mod Options → EPrime's Readouts and turn off Use vanilla readout.

Open Readouts' Options tab from the readout's gear, or choose Options → Mod Options → EPrime's Readouts. Both routes open the same settings window, and the Mod Options route also works from the main menu.
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/08-buffered-rend: Readouts uses cached panel images to reduce drawing work. If it detects a problem displaying them, the panel draws directly instead.

If buffered rendering is disabled after failures, the gear turns amber. Further repeated failures switch to the game's own readout until you load a game again. These fallback changes are recorded in the game log.
help_source.Readouts/Help/4-options/09-the-toolbar-t: Keep the readout toggle in the toolbar brings the button back with a new purpose: clicking it shows or hides the groups. With the groups hidden, the panel keeps only the gear and the search field, and a search still shows its results.
The game has a resource readout button in the toolbar at the bottom right of the screen. Readouts hides it, because the panel has its own way of showing tiers.
The button uses the game's own setting for the categorized readout, so if you switch back to the game's readout later, that setting is whatever you last clicked.
![The counter font option in Display Options](counter-font.png)
Both sizes override the game's tiny-text setting. Changes apply immediately; resource counts stay the same.
You can reach these options from the gear or from Mod Options (see [Panel position and size](topic:panel-position-and-size)).
Counter font size is in Display Options on the Options tab. Choose Tiny or Small. Tiny is the default.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-0b: WorkRoles replaces the vanilla priority grid system with a role system. Instead of assigning priority numbers to work types, you assign a set of named roles to colonists. Behind the scenes, both systems produce an ordered set of jobs that colonists should perform.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-2e: A work type is one vanilla grid column; a job is one specific activity inside it. The Doctoring work type bundles jobs like tending patients and performing surgery:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-4f: Most pre-made roles match the columns of the vanilla priority grid, one role per kind of work colonists can do. The rest are extras the mod adds for more precise assignments: narrower roles like Butcher or Plant Cutter, and bundles like Basics.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-60: Roles hold either whole work types or single jobs: the pre-made ![Doctor chip](chip-doctor.png) role carries the complete Doctoring work type, while Butcher carries only the butchering jobs from Cooking.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-71: Think of a role as a container for jobs. You can edit roles to choose the order of jobs within a role, or stick with the defaults (which closely mirror vanilla behavior).
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-94: ![The Doctoring work type and its jobs](worktype-jobs.png)
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-9a: The stars on a chip are a suitability verdict: how well this colonist fits the role, from red (bad) through grey (neutral) to white and gold (good). [Verdicts](topic:verdicts) has the full scale.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/01-roles.md#b-9b: Chip order decides what gets done first ([Assignment ordering](topic:ordering)), and each chip switches on and off without losing its place ([Role states](topic:states)).
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/02-assigning.md#: Clicking a palette chip with a modifier key held assigns the role to all of them. The modifier decides where the role lands in each row:

- Shift-click puts it last.
- Ctrl+Shift-click puts it right after Basics.
- Alt-click puts it where the [recommendation engine](topic:recommendations) would rank it for that colonist.

- Drag a palette chip onto a colonist's row.
- Shift-click a palette chip to assign it to the selected colonist, or to every selected colonist (see below).
- Click the ![plus button](tex:UI/Buttons/Plus|24) at the end of a colonist's row and pick from the menu.

Dropping a chip also picks its position in the row, so a drag assigns and prioritizes in one motion. The tooltip's Best fits list is a preview of who the [recommendation engine](topic:recommendations) would give it to.
Roles live in the palette at the top of the Colonists tab, clustered by the skill they depend on, plus Everyone and Unskilled clusters for the universal stuff:

Select the colonists first. Click a name to select one, Shift-click another name to select everyone between the two, and Ctrl-click to add or remove single colonists. Ctrl+A selects everyone listed in the table:
![The left part of the role palette](palette-left.png)
Three ways to hand out a role:
Colonists who already hold the role are skipped. While several colonists are selected the [colonist panel](topic:selected-panel) is hidden; click a single colonist to bring it back.
Every palette chip tells you how to use it when hovered:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/03-states.md#b-4: While a role is disabled globally, its chip wears a double strike ![chip with a double strike](chip-state-global-off.png) on every colonist holding it.

Clicking a chip in a colonist's row cycles between on ![enabled chip](chip-state-on.png), off for this colonist ![chip with a single strike](chip-state-off.png), and forced on ![chip with a claim flag](chip-state-forced.png). Off both globally and for the colonist stacks the strikes ![chip with stacked strikes](chip-state-both-off.png), while forced on keeps working even when the role is disabled globally.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/03-states.md#b-6: Handy for roles you keep parked: hand Plant Cutter to half the colony, leave it off globally, and flip one palette chip the day the blight arrives.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/03-states.md#b-9: Clicking a role in the palette toggles it globally, from ![palette chip, enabled](palette-chip-on.png) to ![palette chip, disabled](palette-chip-off.png).
Unsure about a chip? Its tooltip names the state in the framed corner:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/03-states.md#b-c: Toggling never removes the assignment; the chip keeps its place in the row.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/03-states.md#b-d: A role can be turned off globally (for the whole colony) and/or per colonist.
![The role chip tooltip with the state corner framed](chip-tooltip-state.png)
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/04-ordering.md#b: A colonist works their row from left to right, counting enabled roles only:

1. Earlier roles outrank later ones, job for job.
2. Inside a role, earlier jobs come first.
3. A job listed in several roles counts at its earliest position.

RimWorld keeps a separate list for emergency jobs: firefighting, urgent tending and going to bed for emergency treatment. Jobs on that list interrupt sleep, meals and any other job. By default an emergency job goes on that list only when one of the colonist's first five enabled roles covers it. Emergency jobs from later roles run in their normal position. A colonist with Core first and Doctor as their sixth role still interrupts any job for a fire, but treats urgent tending as ordinary doctor work at its position in the row. Moving Core down the row past the fifth position turns firefighting into ordinary work for that colonist too.

Turn off "Only the first 5 roles interrupt for emergencies" on the Options tab to remove this limit. Then every emergency job covered by an enabled role goes on the list, regardless of where the role sits in the row.
Colonists will only perform jobs from the assigned roles. Not assigning a role is equivalent to leaving the vanilla priority grid slot without a number.
Drops work across rows too: drag a chip onto another colonist to move the assignment. Click the trash can icon inside a chip to remove the assignment; the chip leaves the row.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/05-copy-paste.md: Copy one colonist's roles, then paste onto as many others as you like. Order, toggles, everything travels along. Great for cloning a proven setup onto fresh recruits.
The two buttons after a colonist's name copy and paste whole role rows:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/06-selected-pane: Hover any skill for the full story behind its rating:

Every signal the recommendation engine used is listed with its effect and source, so a rating is never a mystery. The panel's right side holds the Recommended Roles list, covered in [Applying single roles](topic:cherry-picking).
The colonist panel at the bottom of the Colonists tab belongs to the selected colonist. It is hidden while [several colonists](topic:assigning) are selected and returns when you click a single one:
Skills are colored by suitability, flames mark passions, and the star pairs are [verdicts](topic:verdicts). The slot under the portrait shows what the colonist is doing right now.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/07-filters.md#b-: The filter row narrows the table without touching any assignments:
Filters combine, and the clear button that appears once anything is active resets the search and the role and job filters while leaving location, grouping, and display choices alone.

- **Search** matches colonist names. Every space-separated term must match, and prefixes widen the hunt: r: or role: searches assigned role names, j: or job: searches the jobs those roles supply. "br r:doc" finds colonists named *br-something* holding a doctor-ish role.
- **Assigned role** lists colonists holding the chosen role, or any non-[blocker](topic:blocker-roles) role that fully covers its jobs.
- **Covered job** lists colonists whose non-blocker roles include the chosen job.
- **Location** picks which colony supplies the table: the current map, everywhere, a settlement, or the ship. Colonists out with a caravan count under the place they left from.
A filter never hides a selected colonist. When one would, the selection is cleared and the first colonist still listed is selected instead.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/08-display.md#b-: ![Rows with initials aligned in grid columns](initials-grid-row.png)
The button beside Display switches between two layouts. Its face shows the active one: a brick wall for chips stacked at their natural widths, or a grid for chips aligned in equal-width columns.
Click a column header to sort the table by that skill, click its X to remove the column. Values carry the same passion flames and suitability colors as the colonist panel.
The right side of the filter row holds the view controls:
The Display button picks what assigned chips show. Full names:
Grouping only arranges rows; the filters still decide who is listed, and with Colony Groups installed its groups appear as an option.
The Skills button adds up to three skill columns to the table:

Full-name grid columns are sized for eight leading letters, and a longer name fades out at the edge of its chip. A name gets more room only when it needs it to stay distinct from a similar role name. The chip tooltip always shows the whole name. Right-click the layout button to choose Short, Medium or Long instead, which size every column the same, or Full to show every name whole.
Group by splits the table into collapsible sections, here by gender:
![Rows with icons aligned in grid columns](icons-grid-row.png)
More display switches live on the Options tab:
All of these are personal preferences: in multiplayer each player keeps their own, and nothing here changes any assignment.
