help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/09-bill-roles.md: Picking a specific worker clears the role restriction, and picking a role clears the worker.

Only colonists actively holding the role work the bill, and a [conditional role](topic:conditional-roles) brings its rules along. This shines when a bill needs a particular skill mix: a drug production bill restricted to a role that combines crafting and intellectual jobs always lands on someone qualified.
![The role option in a bill's worker dropdown](bill-role-filter.png)
Work bills can be restricted to a role instead of a single worker:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/10-priority-grid: Two related switches live on the Options tab:

The first is vanilla's own "manual priorities" toggle (it lives here because WorkRoles replaced the tab that hosted it). The second maps the mod's sequential priorities onto the vanilla 0 to 4 range for other mods that read them.
Missing the old numbers? The two small numbered buttons ![the priority grid buttons](priority-grid-buttons.png) above the table's scrollbar open a read-only priority grid, one for each view:

The grid shows the priorities WorkRoles computed for every listed colonist, respecting the active filters. The button at the top switches between the mod's raw ranks and the familiar vanilla 0 to 4 view.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/1-basics/11-keyboard.md#b: The colonist table reads the keyboard while no text field has focus:

- Up and Down arrows select the previous or next colonist. Hold Shift to extend the selection instead.
- Home and End jump to the first or last. Hold Ctrl to ignore group sections.
- Page Up and Page Down move a page (or group) at a time.
- Ctrl+A selects every colonist listed in the table, collapsed groups included.
- Ctrl+C copies the selected colonist's role row and Ctrl+V pastes it, the same as the [copy and paste buttons](topic:copy-paste).
- Ctrl+F puts the cursor in the search box.
The six movement bindings live under WorkRoles in the game's keyboard configuration, ready to be remapped.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/01-role-tree.md: Above the groups sit the display controls, covered under [Organizing](topic:tree-views):
[Conditional roles](topic:conditional-roles) collect here automatically and return to their stored group when their rules are cleared.
The left side of the Roles tab lists every role in the colony. Most of it is your own named groups, like this one:

The indentation above is auto-nesting: a role whose jobs fully cover another shows the covered role indented beneath it, so Handyman sits under Builder, and Fix Roof under Handyman. A covered role can appear under several parents; the repeated appearances are extra listings of the same role, and its own group remains the real home.

Groups have no editor screen because they need none: assign a role to a new group name and the group appears, move its last role away and it vanishes. Drag roles to reorder them inside a group or to move them between groups; click a role to open it in the [editor](topic:role-editor).
And first among the groups gathers everything rule-driven:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/02-managing-rol: The buttons under the role tree manage the roster:

New starts an empty role, Copy duplicates the selected one (a good starting point for a variant), and Delete removes it from every colonist after a confirmation. Every seeded role can be edited, renamed, or deleted; [Restore Defaults](topic:restore-defaults) brings any of them back later.
Rename from the editor header next to the role's name. Names must be unique, mostly so future-you knows which "Hauler 2" was the good one.
For a normal role the header covers the everyday settings: rename beside the name, [icon and color](topic:icons-colors), the [group](topic:role-groups) the role lives in, and the age groups allowed to hold it. Roles whose jobs use skills also list them here, derived automatically from the [selected jobs](topic:picking-jobs).
The switches on the right turn a role into one of the special [role types](topic:role-types); for a normal role they all stay off.
Selecting a role opens it in the editor:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/04-picking-jobs: To move or remove several rows at once, select them first: click a row, Shift-click another to select everything between the two, or Ctrl-click to add or remove single rows. The header shows how many rows are selected and gains move and remove buttons for the whole selection. The buttons on the rows themselves are inactive until a single row is selected again:
Selections land in the ordered list on the right:

Click the mark beside a work type to toggle all of it; expand the type to toggle individual jobs. ![in](tex:UI/Widgets/CheckOn|20) means in this role, ![out](tex:UI/Widgets/CheckOff|20) means out, and ![partially](tex:UI/Widgets/CheckPartial|20) on a work type means only some of its jobs are in.

A work-type row covers all of its jobs, including ones other mods add later. Jobs picked individually get their own rows and can be dragged into any order, which is exactly the [priority order](topic:ordering) holders will use. A dimmed row adds nothing new (everything it covers is already claimed above it); move it up or remove it.
A role's job list is built from the Available Jobs tree:
![Three selected rows with the header buttons](selected-jobs-multi.png)
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/05-icons-colors: Click the icon square beside the role's name to pick a new one:
Colors come from the palette in the editor's top-right corner:

The left block holds mild built-ins, the bright grid is the shared palette, and the plus row underneath stores custom colors. Click an empty plus to define one, right-click a filled slot to redefine it. Custom colors are shared across all roles, so a recolor updates every role using that slot.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/06-role-types.m: Most roles you touch will be Regular: a plain list of jobs like Doctor or Cook. The editor's switches turn a role into something else:

There is also a soft kind with no switch: a regular role whose jobs fully cover other roles shows those roles nested underneath it in the [role tree](topic:tree-views). Basics and Grunt work like that.

- **Auto-assign**: newcomers receive the role automatically. See [Auto-assign](topic:auto-assign).
- **Blocker**: the role forbids its jobs instead of allowing them. See [Blocker roles](topic:blocker-roles).
- **Conditional**: the role switches itself by hour or place. See [Conditional roles](topic:conditional-roles).
- **Composite**: the role bundles other roles instead of jobs. See [Composite roles](topic:composite-roles).
Core, Basics, and Grunt ship with it on, which is why fresh colonists arrive with a working row instead of an empty one. Flip the switch in the editor to change which roles greet newcomers.

Auto-assign is the welcome committee: recruits, wanderers, and anyone else who joins receives the role automatically. A newcomer outside the role's age groups is skipped, so separate child and adult roles can both use it. Birthdays follow the same age groups: a colonist who grows into an auto-assign role receives it, and a colonist who grows past any role they hold loses it. Where such a role lands in a recommended row is governed by its [role options](topic:role-options), like any other role.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/08-blocker-role: A blocker turns a role inside out: its jobs become forbidden instead of allowed.
![The role type switches with Blocker on](blocker-toggles.png)
Colonists genetically terrified of fire receive Pyrophobe automatically, placed where it belongs.

Everything after the blocker in a colonist's row is affected; roles placed before it still win. The seeded Pyrophobe role holds only Firefighting: put it before Core and that colonist never fights fires, put a Firefighter role before it to make an exception.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/09-conditional-: A conditional role switches itself on and off by rules:

The hour strip sets when the role applies (paint hours off to carve out downtime), and the location picker sets where: settlements, caravans, or a named ship. A role becomes conditional the moment any rule is set, and gathers under the automatic Conditional Roles group in the tree.

While a rule suppresses the role, its chips dim and their tooltips say why ("Off: outside active hours"). The seeded setup has none of these; the classic homemade example is a mining role that only applies while the colonist is away from home.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/3-editing/10-composite-ro: Holders do the member roles' jobs in the member order, as one assignment. A composite bundling Farmer and Handler gives you a single chip for the full outdoor package.
Several rows in the Member Roles list can be selected, moved and removed at once, the same way as in the [Selected Jobs list](topic:picking-jobs).
A composite role bundles whole roles instead of jobs. Flip the Composite switch and the job panes become role panes:
House rules: members must be regular roles without hour or location rules, and a composite cannot contain another composite. Editing a member role updates every composite bundling it.
Work added by other mods shows up in the job tree automatically, no compatibility patch required.

When new work appears mid-game, WorkRoles extends or creates roles to cover it and posts a message naming what changed. Jobs from AllowTool and Keyz' Allow Utilities slot into the matching seeded roles on their own.

If a job ends up in no role at all, the editor shows an amber warning so nothing silently goes undone. And when a mod leaves your game, its jobs go dormant inside their roles until it returns or the job is manually removed from the role definition.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/4-organizing/01-role-grou: Groups are pure organization: they never affect what anyone works on.

Click a group header to collapse or expand it. The editor's Group button moves the selected role by menu, and its New option creates a fresh group; [dragging](topic:role-tree) in the tree does the same by hand.
The role tree keeps your roster in named, collapsible groups:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/4-organizing/02-automatic: A role keeps its stored group underneath: clear the rules (or revert the composite) and it returns to wherever it lived before. The automatic groups exist so the special roles are always easy to find, however the rest of the tree is arranged.
Two groups curate themselves. Roles with hour or location rules gather under Conditional Roles, and composite roles gather under Composite Roles.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/4-organizing/03-tree-view: Flat view lists every role exactly where its group puts it, nothing inferred. Both views show the same roles.
The Display toggle above the tree switches nesting:

Nested view shows [auto-nesting](topic:role-tree), with covered roles indented under the role covering them. A dashed swatch marks a role shown under a parent while belonging to another group; the tooltip names its real home.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/4-organizing/04-list-filt: Both only filter the view; selections and assignments stay untouched.

Two controls above the tree find roles fast. The search box matches role names as you type. The job filter lists only roles containing the chosen job, which answers the eternal question "who on earth is allowed to slaughter the alpacas".
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/4-organizing/05-palette-m: The role palette on the Colonists tab can be arranged two ways, chosen at the bottom of the Options tab's display settings:
A per-player choice, like everything on that panel.
Skills mode clusters roles by the skill they lean on (the default, shown throughout this manual). Groups mode mirrors your own [role groups](topic:role-groups) instead, in the order you keep them.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/01-reco: The recommendation engine reads what your colonists are good at and what the colony needs, then proposes a role row for each of them.

With supported Vivi versions, gathering recommendations use the worker's actual gathering speed and yield. A human with a Vivi straw can gather honey and pollen; a multiuse brush enables plant gathering. Equipping or removing these tools updates capability while paused. A worker who can perform some gathering recipes remains eligible for gathering; unavailable recipes stay excluded from training choices. Unknown Vivi builds or custom gathering rules retain existing behavior.

Precepts that oppose work lower its recommendation score. A suitable willing colonist is more likely to get it, while an opposed colonist can still cover essential work. A verified refusal or missing capability makes that work ineligible. Skill ratings still describe aptitude; Best fits lists that raw aptitude among capable colonists, while the colony recommendation also accounts for aversions and demand.
You can see its opinion everywhere. Palette tooltips list the best fits for every role:

The engine suggests; applying is yours, one role at a time ([cherry-picking](topic:cherry-picking)) or wholesale ([Fix My Colony](topic:fix-my-colony)). The exception is [Auto-optimize](topic:auto-optimize): switch it on and Fix My Colony runs automatically every in-game hour, across all your colonies.

Its evidence is called signals: burning passions, gene aptitudes, traits, skill expertise, and the best skills in the colony. On top of that it enforces colony needs, so essential roles like Doctor and Cook always land on somebody, ideally the somebody with the talent.
These are recommendation inputs. Conditional roles continue to control when and where an assigned role is active.

Two roles get special handling. Hunter is recommended to anyone carrying a ranged weapon (hunting trains Shooting), placed earlier for poor shots and later for sharpshooters whose time is worth more elsewhere. An aversion to hunting also places Hunter later in the row. Mechanitor is recommended only to colonists with a mechlink, however good the other crafters are, and its Best fits list follows the same rule.

The engine considers all eligible roles and orders them automatically for each colonist. Role Options on the Recommendations tab lists every role except those you have excluded. To prevent a role from ever being recommended, add it to **Excluded roles** at the top of that tab. Exclusions take precedence over colony needs and special handling, while existing pinned assignments stay protected. See [Ordering and exclusions](topic:recommendation-order) for details.

**Use robot and mech coverage in human recommendations** is a separate per-save option, also off by default. It counts accepted mechanical assignments toward staffing, allowing a fully covered duty to replace its last human specialist. Each worker supplies one primary duty; fallback roles add no independent staffing credit. Restricted areas, blocked work, insufficient skills and Quality Jobs restrictions on robot work prevent full coverage. A robot that can only clean does not replace a combined cleaning-and-hauling role.

Selected human training below its target and pinned assignments stay protected. Routine charging retains coverage; deactivation, lost control or leaving Work mode removes it. Updated recommendations propose human replacements, while Auto-optimize applies them at its normal hourly boundary when enabled. With integration off, robot and mech rows do not affect human recommendations.

When robot and mech rows are enabled, their suggestions use current skills and executable work, without human passions or learning paths. Their accepted primary duty stays in place, including an explicitly assigned excluded role; change that duty manually. Suggestions for additional work respect exclusions. You choose their assignments; Auto-optimize continues to apply human recommendations only.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/02-verd: The chip tooltip states the verdict in words:

Red stars warn: one for Poor, a second red star for Awful. Grey is Neutral. White stars approve: one for Strong, two for Great, and gold marks Exceptional. The tinted chip with the warning marker flags a capability problem on top of the rating; hover it for the reason.
Three Options-tab switches control where verdict stars appear:
A verdict is the engine's one-glance rating of a colonist for a role, shown as star pairs on chips:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/03-read: The Source column is worth a glance when another mod's genes or skills are in play. Chips in the Recommended Roles list explain themselves the same way: their tooltips state why the role was picked, whether it fills a colony minimum, arrived through a training path, or scored on signals alone.
No verdict is a black box. Hover a skill in the colonist panel and the tooltip lays out every signal behind the rating:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/04-cher: Click any chip to assign just that role, exactly where the engine would place it. The panel mixes three kinds of chip: a normal chip is a role the engine wants to add, a dimmed chip is already assigned (clicking it changes nothing), and a red border marks a current role the engine would remove.
The Recommended Roles list in the colonist panel shows the engine's proposed row for the selected colonist:
Cherry-picking is the gentlest way to use the engine: take the ideas you like and ignore the rest, nothing needs [pinning](topic:pinning) first.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/05-make: The ![Make It So button](make-it-so-btn.png) button under the Recommended Roles list applies the whole displayed set to the selected colonist in one click.

Roles the engine did not recommend are removed, and the rest land in the recommended order. [Pinned](topic:pinning) assignments are preserved, including roles in [Excluded roles](topic:recommendation-order). Handy when one colonist's row has drifted.
For the colony-wide version with a preview, see [Fix My Colony](topic:fix-my-colony).
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/06-fix-: Nothing happens blind: a preview lists every colonist's proposed row first, with a checkbox per colonist to leave individuals out.

Apply performs exactly what the preview shows. Pinned assignments are preserved, even when their role or a composite member is in [Excluded roles](topic:recommendation-order). Unpinned excluded roles are removed; blockers and rule-carrying roles are otherwise retained.
The button in the window's top-right corner reworks everyone at once:
Colony planning is per location, so the button asks for a single settlement or ship in the [location filter](topic:filters) when the table currently mixes several.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/07-pinn: Right-click a chip and pick Pin. A pinned chip wears a pin marker:

Pinned assignments are off limits to the recommendation engine: [Make It So](topic:make-it-so), [Fix My Colony](topic:fix-my-colony), and [Auto-optimize](topic:auto-optimize) preserve them, even when their role or a composite member is in [Excluded roles](topic:recommendation-order). Pin the assignments you set by hand and let the engine argue about the rest.
[Conditional roles](topic:conditional-roles) need no pin: rule-driven assignments are left alone, along with blockers, unless excluded. [What is never touched](topic:untouched) has the full list.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/08-auto: With several colonies, mind the fine print: the switch is global and optimizes all of them, every hour. This is a per-savegame setting.

Enabling shows a confirmation preview of the first pass. While active, the Fix My Colony and Make It So buttons hide (the machine has the wheel), though assigning, reordering, and pinning by hand still work.
For the fully hands-off colony, the Options tab offers hourly automation:

While it is on, [Fix My Colony](topic:fix-my-colony) runs automatically for every colony at the top of each in-game hour. Nothing is written when a colonist already matches the recommendation, and [pinned](topic:pinning) assignments survive every pass, including when their role or a composite member is in [Excluded roles](topic:recommendation-order).
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/09-unto:
- [Pinned](topic:pinning) assignments, your explicit "hands off".
- [Blocker roles](topic:blocker-roles), because forbidding something was a decision.
- [Conditional roles](topic:conditional-roles), which their rules manage already.
- Every role of a downed colonist.

Their non-excluded roles and pinned assignments stay as they are until they recover, and nothing they hold counts toward colony needs, so the engine covers those needs with other colonists. Every chip in their Recommended Roles list says so:

Make It So, Fix My Colony, and Auto-optimize normally preserve four kinds of assignment:

**Pinned assignments remain protected even when excluded.** If an unpinned role or one of its composite members is excluded, applying recommendations removes that assignment. See [Recommendation order](topic:recommendation-order).
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/10-reco: Rescuer, Firefighter, Patient, Bedrest, and Laborer are excluded by default because Core and Basics already cover their work. Existing saves receive these defaults once when updated. Removing a role from the panel is respected on later loads. To add the defaults back, choose **Default excluded roles** in [Restore Defaults](topic:restore-defaults).

You can still assign excluded roles manually. Editing the exclusion list does not alter current assignments. Applying recommendations removes unpinned excluded roles from the affected colonists. **Pinned assignments remain protected**, even if their role or a composite member is excluded. A kept pinned assignment is your existing choice, not a new recommendation.

- A [training role](topic:training-paths) lands directly after its path's target, so Nurse and Medic follow Doctor.
- A role fully covered by another sits right after the role covering it, the way Hauler follows Grunt.
- **Hunter keeps its shooting-skill placement:** poor shots hunt earlier and better shots hunt later, because their time is worth more elsewhere. An individually pinned assignment remains protected.
[Role Options](topic:role-options) below lists all non-excluded roles. Excluding a role hides its options without erasing them; removing the exclusion makes those options available again.

Recommendations are ordered automatically for each colonist. The engine uses its built-in order alongside suitability, colony importance, time demand, training paths, and coverage. Custom roles fit into that order using the game's work priorities. The former colony-wide ordering panel has been removed, and saved custom orders no longer affect recommendations.

The **Excluded roles** panel at the top of the Recommendations tab controls which roles must never be recommended. Use Add Role to exclude a role, or click its chip's remove icon to allow recommendations again.

Exclusions apply across the save, including [Fix My Colony](topic:fix-my-colony) and [Auto-optimize](topic:auto-optimize). They override colony demand, training paths, automatic and special roles, composite substitution, and unpinned retained assignments, including those on incapacitated workers. Excluding a composite leaves its eligible member roles available; excluding a member prevents it from returning through a recommended composite.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/11-role: The seeded roles come pre-tuned; these options are how you disagree.

- **Colony importance**: Important promotes the role above same-strength production work in a colonist's row, Optional pushes it toward the end.
- **Time demand**: part-time duties sit above full-time work of equal strength, opportunistic filler drops last.
- **Repeat champion penalty**: discourages one overachiever (the engine's champion pick) from anchoring every role; switch it off for roles where that is fine.
- **Assignment Scaling**: the colony minimum is how many holders the engine must find, coverage is the percentage of colonists it should aim for.
- **Skills**: work types and used, trained, and gated skills are derived from the role's jobs. Add Skill adds a hard gate: a colonist with that skill disabled is never recommended the role.
- **Training Path**: covered in [its own topic](topic:training-paths).
Role Options lists all roles except those in Excluded roles, in alphabetical order. Expand a role to tune how the engine treats it:
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/5-recommendations/12-trai: Each band is a role with the skill range where it applies, and bands may overlap: here Jailor covers Social 0 to 4, Warden takes over from 4, and Caretaker joins from 6 without replacing Warden. A colonist at Social 2 is recommended Jailor, at 5 Warden, and at 10 both Warden and Caretaker.

Drag a band's ends to resize its range, drag the middle to move it. Where bands do not overlap the later role replaces the earlier; where they do, the roles complement. Roles that train none of the target's skills warn before being added; you can still add one when a mod changes what grants XP.

- **Champion selection** decides who anchors each role.
- **Training path and optional target** options govern when paths activate and when optional multi-skill roles are worth recommending.
- **Lead diversification** spreads training leads across colonists.
- **Final role ordering** decides how a colonist's recommended roles are sequenced.
- **Hunter placement** sets the shooting cutoffs for Hunter's dynamic slot.
Every dial explains itself in place, and each section's Reset restores the defaults after adventurous experiments.

The right side of the Recommendations tab holds the engine's dials, folded into five sections. Most players will never need to tune these settings, but the knobs are available to those that would like to tweak the recommendations.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/6-advanced/01-under-the-h: Everything recomputes when assignments or roles change, then sits in a cache. Conditional roles additionally refresh at hour boundaries and when a colonist changes location. Emergency jobs like firefighting go through the game's emergency work pass when one of the colonist's first five enabled roles covers them; the rest run in their normal position. With "Only the first 5 roles interrupt for emergencies" off, every covered emergency job uses that pass.

WorkRoles keeps vanilla's priority storage populated from your roles (mapped onto the familiar 0 to 4 range while the vanilla-range option is on, the default), which is why removing the mod is safe: the vanilla Work tab returns, populated with your roles converted to priorities. Adding the mod to an existing save converts the other way.

Each colonist's ordered roles compile into one strict job order, fed to the game through the same lists vanilla job selection already reads. Work behavior matches a hand-tuned priority grid, with no tick patches or per-frame work.

help_source.WorkRoles/Help/6-advanced/03-restore-def: **Default excluded roles** adds Rescuer, Firefighter, Patient, Bedrest, and Laborer back to the Excluded roles panel if you removed them. Other exclusions stay as you set them. You can remove restored exclusions again afterward.

The preview lists everything restorable: missing pre-made roles, your own job edits, jobs that other mods moved away, default groups, colors, holder settings, and default exclusions. Check only what you want; items that would overwrite your own edits are highlighted in warning colors.
Deleted Doctor in a fit of confidence? Restore Defaults on the Roles tab brings the factory settings back, piece by piece:
Colonists keep their overall jobs through a restore, so nobody stops working while you repent.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/6-advanced/04-compatibili: Unknown framework builds preserve existing eligibility and report that their rules are unsupported. Restrictions hidden inside arbitrary jobs cannot be detected safely by trying jobs during recommendation capture. Supported Vivi versions provide equipment-dependent gathering speed, yield and eligibility. Unknown Vivi builds, custom gathering rules and unverified Ratkin-specific rules retain existing behavior; no race or xenotype name is used to guess a restriction.

Recommendations also read declared work tags, required capacities, precept opposition, and verified ordinary-mining refusals. For audited Humanoid Alien Races builds on RimWorld 1.6 and 1.7, they use the framework's actual work-giver and recipe restrictions. Different races using those rules benefit from the same integration. A blocked recipe does not remove other usable recipes from the role or count as a way to train its skill.
Some mods require priorities in the range 0 to 4, so if you have issues with other mods make sure the "Report vanilla 0-4 priorities to other mods" option is enabled.

Mech priority mods such as Mech Work Tab can manage workers with no WorkRoles assignments. If you enable robot and mech support, WorkRoles owns work ordering for mechanical workers with assigned roles too. Turn support off in Options to restore native ordering for all of them; their saved roles remain dormant.

Work and jobs from other mods are picked up automatically, and several mods get deeper integration: Vanilla Skills Expanded and Alpha Skills expertise feed the recommendation signals, More Than Capable's hated work becomes an Awful signal, Colony Groups appears as a grouping option, and multi-floor mods treat stacked floors as one location.
Mods that only read priorities are fine; they see the values WorkRoles computed.

Optional work and skill mods can supply additional job profiles. These profiles identify the skills a job uses and trains, and may refine its primary recommendation skill when the relevant mods are installed. WorkRoles leaves job eligibility, designations and execution to the mods that provide them. These integrations add no required mod dependencies.

Add-ons that patch existing work givers still use the same roles and job ordering. Animal-handling roles, for example, continue to use Animals for recommendations. Conditional experience gains in another skill depend on the add-on's eligibility rules; they do not create a general training path for every colonist assigned to that work.

Two families do clash. Other Work tab replacements (Work Tab forks, Better Work Tab and friends) fight over the same UI. Priority-setting mods (Free Will, PriorityMaster and similar) fight over the same data: WorkRoles owns priorities for managed colonists, so their writes are blocked. When that happens a one-time notice names the mod and suggests the role-based way to get the same effect.

Charging remains native behavior and needs no Recharge role. Biotech provides charge limits in each control group. Misc. Robots uses its own automatic return thresholds; clicking the charge percentage in its Robots tab requests an immediate recharge. WorkRoles does not change those thresholds.

**Show robots and mechs in Colonists** is a per-save option, off by default. It adds Biotech mechs, Misc. Robots and Misc. Robots++ to the existing table. Assign roles there; use their native tabs for control groups, areas, activation and charging. Roles only order work the worker can actually perform. Humanlike androids continue to use the ordinary colonist rules.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/6-advanced/05-multiplayer: WorkRoles is fully RimWorld Multiplayer compatible. Every change that matters (role edits, assignments, toggles, pins, tuning) travels as a synced command, so all players stay in perfect agreement about who does what.
Presentation stays personal: display modes, verdict stars, and groupings are yours alone and never touch the shared state.
help_source.WorkRoles/Help/6-advanced/06-screen-size: WorkRoles is designed for a game screen of at least 1536x864. The game screen is your resolution divided by the UI scale, so 1920x1080 at UI scale 1.25 matches it exactly.
A smaller screen still works: the window fills the screen, some labels are shortened and the tabs need more scrolling. Lowering the UI scale in the game's options gives the window more room.
The selected-colonist panel uses two columns for the usual twelve skills. Mods that add skills get a third column with a narrower recommendations panel. More than eighteen skills add extra rows.
When the recommended roles do not all fit, scroll inside their panel to see the rest. The Make It So button stays in view.
